frames.name: Manual Journal Preparation (MJV)
frames.win: Month-end close · Manual · BlackLine, SAP, Email
frames.owner: Controlling (Embedded Finance, GFS Controller, GFS Manager) with Business requestors and GFS FP&A
ctl: Embedded Finance (CFO / FC / CBP) approval of cost details

GFS Manager review and approval before posting

ch.t: Heavy reliance on manual journals (MJV) and human intervention during close activities
Errors, inconsistencies and audit scrutiny risks arising from manual corrections
Focus on downstream symptom correction rather than upstream root-cause prevention
Lack of consistent accounting interpretation and governance across markets
High volume of rework and correction journals impacting productivity
Competing priorities between manual close activities and automation initiatives

tpi.t: Month-End Close Transformation - MJV Reduction & Global MJV Playbook Deployment: deploy the Global MJV Playbook across APAC to standardise journal governance and accounting treatment
MJV Dashboard giving 100% visibility of APAC journals, root causes and preventable journal trends; root-cause analysis and prevention framework to eliminate recurring correction journals
Target ~30% reduction in preventable MJVs and ~250 hours annual productivity gain; shift from reactive correction to a prevention-driven, Right-First-Time close

up.w: Manual journal requests (judgmental journals during month-end close)
Coupa accruals as preventable manual journals

down.w: Manual journals posted in BlackLine during month-end close (before the GL closes at WD+2)
Management P&L review after posting (FP&A Comm or FP&A Ops - owner to confirm, register gap 56)

procs.name: Manual Journal Request (MJV)
inbox: A manual journal is needed during month-end close: globally SOP-approved (stock provision, bonus and unutilised-leave accruals) or preventable (corrections / reclasses, manual accruals, Coupa accruals, COBOU, indirect tax)
procs.outdoc: Approved manual journals posted in BlackLine during month-end close; management P&L reviewed
procs.outnote: Hands to R2R-01 SAP Close - journals must be posted before the GL closes at WD+2

steps.d: The Business requestor sends the manual journal request to Embedded Finance. Journal types: globally SOP-approved journals (stock provision, bonus accruals, unutilised leave accruals) and preventable journals (corrections / reclasses, manual accruals, Coupa accruals, COBOU, indirect tax).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 1; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.01

steps.t: Review and approve the cost details
steps.d: Embedded Finance (CFO / FC / CBP) reviews and approves the cost details of the request.
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 2; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.02

steps.d: Embedded Finance decides whether a manual journal is required; if not, the request is rejected and the requestor informed.
steps.ex: Cost already captured by an automated accrual - no journal needed
steps.yes: Continue to D2 - GSOP compliance check
steps.no: Reject and inform the requestor - end

steps.d: The GFS Controller checks the journal complies with the Global SOP; non-compliant requests are rejected and the requestor informed. MIRO feedback: no separate compliance review step - the journal is posted directly into BlackLine after manager review.
steps.ex: Accrual request without the supporting calculation required by the GSOP
steps.yes: Continue to step 3 - prepare and post
steps.no: Step 2a - reject and inform the requestor
steps.src: MJV process flow deck decision 2.2; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.03

fix.d: The GFS Controller rejects the non-compliant request and informs the requestor (deck: end).
pp: Lack of consistent accounting interpretation and governance across markets

steps.d: The GFS Controller prepares the journal and posts it in BlackLine (to SAP).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 3; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.04
out: Journal posted before the GL close
pp: Heavy reliance on manual journals (MJV) and human intervention during close activities
Errors, inconsistencies and audit scrutiny risks arising from manual corrections
Competing priorities between manual close activities and automation initiatives

steps.d: The GFS Manager reviews and approves the journal; it is posted directly into BlackLine after manager review (MIRO feedback: no compliance review step after this).
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 4; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.05; MIRO feedback 5

steps.d: GFS FP&A reviews the management P&L after the journals are posted.
steps.src: MJV process flow deck step 5; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.06

steps.d: If the management P&L review finds an issue, the GFS Controller corrects the journal and it goes back through prepare, post and approval (deck: back to step 3); otherwise the journal stands.
steps.ex: Accrual posted to the wrong cost centre
steps.no: Step 6 - correct the journal, then back to prepare and post (step 3)

fix.d: The GFS Controller corrects the journal; it goes back to prepare and post (step 3) and through the manager approval again.
fix.src: MJV process flow deck step 6; process register (all towers), row CTRL-01.01.07
pp: Errors, inconsistencies and audit scrutiny risks arising from manual corrections
Focus on downstream symptom correction rather than upstream root-cause prevention
High volume of rework and correction journals impacting productivity

frames.name: Statutory Audit
frames.win: Annual · Manual · KPMG Clara / KCC, Wdesk / Workiva, Email, SAP (P13)
frames.owner: Controlling with Embedded Finance, Tax, all process towers and the auditors (KPMG / Deloitte)
ctl: Audit scope and timeline agreed at planning
PBC evidence routed through the KPMG Clara / KCC repository
P13 audit adjustments validated and approved before posting

ch.t: Late stakeholder alignment and incomplete planning information
Multiple process tower coordination for walkthroughs
High manual effort, duplicate requests and incorrect request routing for PBCs
Large sample sizes, multi-tower dependencies and repeated follow-ups
Multiple review rounds and version control; inconsistent use of Wdesk / Workiva and late access, so queries come by email and Controllers re-key them into Wdesk for Deloitte Stat
Quality issues in the financial statements prepared by SG Deloitte (disclosure errors, casting, cross-referencing, balance presentation) causing extra review effort and revision cycles
Tracking adjustments, supporting documentation and manual retained-earnings reconciliation
Country-specific statutory requirements create admin work

tpi.t: End-to-end audit support model: centralised KPMG planning model and 'test once, use often'; centralised walkthrough repository
KPMG Clara / KCC central repository with direct process-owner routing and an owner matrix; centralised audit testing by KL and Group teams
Keep to a 3x financial statement revision approach, tracked and monitored; standardised P13 governance and templates; improved filing governance and escalation

pp: Late stakeholder alignment, incomplete planning information
Multiple process tower coordination
High manual effort, duplicate requests, incorrect request routing
Large sample sizes, multi-tower dependencies, repeated follow-ups
Multiple review rounds and version control; Wdesk / Workiva access and usage issues; FS quality issues from SG Deloitte
Tracking adjustments, documentation, manual reconciliation
Country-specific statutory requirements

up.w: PBC evidence from the process towers and local teams
Draft statutory financial statements prepared by SG Deloitte
up.src: workbook · Financial Statement Review pain point 3

down.w: Walkthroughs, PBC evidence, query responses, reviewed financial statements
Statutory accounts filed before the statutory deadlines
Audit adjustments (P13) posted; retained earnings reconciled

steps.d: Support the auditor walkthroughs and explain the key finance processes and controls across the process towers.

steps.d: Coordinate the collection and submission of audit evidence (PBCs) from the process towers and local teams into the KPMG Clara / KCC repository.

steps.d: Coordinate the responses to audit samples, information requests and follow-up queries across the towers.

Inconsistent use of Wdesk / Workiva and late access - queries raised by email and re-keyed into Wdesk

rows.t: Cross-tower PBC taxonomy and supporting-document standard
rows.act: Create one PBC category set, mandatory metadata standard, naming convention and supporting-document checklist so requests are comparable, correctly routed and batch-ready.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, P2P, R2R, O2C, Tax, FP&A, CAPEX: Cross-tower PBC taxonomy and supporting-document standard.
rows.rem: A standard PBC will be uploaded in KPMG KCC

rows.t: Direct process-owner routing and owner matrix
rows.act: Maintain an owner matrix that routes routine requests directly to the responsible tower, leaving Controllers to handle technical accounting questions and cross-tower exceptions.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, all process towers: Direct process-owner routing and owner matrix.
rows.rem: All the requests will be assigned  to respective process tower PIC via KPMG KCC

rows.act: Use approved scheduled exports, SAP jobs or controlled desktop automation to produce trial balance, GL and ageing listings across requested entities and report types in batches.
rows.xc: Yes — Audit support, R2R, O2C, SAP/platform team: High-volume SAP listing batch extraction.
rows.rem: This has to implement by Process Tower. Alternatively, is to provide Tcode to KPMG Central team to extract at their end.

rows.t: Bulk Coupa invoice and attachment retrieval
rows.act: Process the requested invoice population together through an approved API or controlled automation, producing found, missing and failed-item logs instead of one-by-one downloads.
rows.xc: Yes — Audit support, P2P, Coupa/platform team: Bulk Coupa invoice and attachment retrieval.
rows.rem: Understood TDT team previously develop this tool to extract bulk invoices. Can explore to extend to P2P/O2C team

rows.act: Create standard SharePoint folders, file names, manifests and KCC upload-ready packages that link each document to its request and sample ID.
rows.xc: Yes — Audit support, process towers, Controlling: Governed evidence package automation.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future
rows.rem: For this 1st year transition, suggest to KIV and observe first. This could be duplicate effort since we are expecting PT to upload supporting directly into KCC.

rows.act: Check sample coverage, identifiers, duplicates, readability and reconciliation where applicable; route only missing or failed items for human resolution.
rows.xc: Yes — Audit support, process towers, Controlling: Deterministic evidence validation.
rows.rem: Can you explain further? Reason being is that data will be stored at KPMG KCC, rather than AZ platform.

rows.act: Show KCC status, ageing, owner, missing evidence, extraction failures and clarification reasons in one view while process towers execute routine requests directly.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, all towers: Cross-tower audit governance dashboard.
rows.rem: This data can be obtained through KPMG KCC site

rows.act: Create a standard alert and triage route for potential statutory-audit issues or adjustments, recording owner, entity, impact, evidence and due date before late-cycle escalation.
rows.xc: Yes — CAPEX, Controlling, all towers: Early audit-risk signal workflow.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future
rows.rem: Controlling has plan to develop an audit adjustment dashboard to identify recurring audit issues before the next audit cycle commence

rows.t: Consolidated auditor query and inter-office confirmation protocol
rows.act: Maintain one register for original and follow-up KPMG questions and test inter-office confirmation for eligible intercompany balances to reduce duplicate evidence requests.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, FP&A Ops, KPMG, relevant towers: Consolidated auditor query and inter-office confirmation protocol.
rows.rem: KPMG UK team is working on developing a DA around intercompany matrix. It could be a cross team collaboration but need to get Hammond/Simon's alignment

rows.act: Assess the PH10 SAP extraction script as a reusable pattern, then add approved Coupa/API routes, standard manifests and found/missing/failed logs for other evidence types.
rows.xc: Yes — O2C, P2P, R2R, Audit support: Reusable evidence-extraction factory.
rows.rem: Can you elaborate further on this?

rows.act: Classify free-text requests, suggest PBC category and owner, identify likely duplicates and draft a routing summary for authorised review.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers, audit support: AI-assisted request triage.

rows.act: Use AI to support readability checks and manifest consistency and to draft exception summaries, while deterministic checks remain authoritative for identifiers, duplicates and sample coverage.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers: AI-assisted evidence quality review.
rows.rem: Can you explain further? Reason being is that data will be stored at KPMG KCC, rather than AZ platform.

rows.act: Summarise comments, classify recurring clarification reasons and surface high-failure request types so the taxonomy, checklist and training can be improved over time.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers, audit support: AI recurring-findings and clarification insight.
rows.rem: Can you explain further? Reason being is that data will be stored at KPMG KCC, rather than AZ platform.

rows.t: Direct tower ownership with Controller exception support
rows.act: Make process towers accountable for routine PBC completion and KCC submission; reserve Controller capacity for technical accounting, cross-tower escalation and complex auditor queries.
rows.xc: Yes — All process towers, Controlling: Direct tower ownership with Controller exception support.
rows.rem: All the requests will be assigned  to respective process tower PIC via KPMG KCC

rows.act: Compare new KCC requests with open and completed items and suggest likely duplicates or reusable evidence for process-owner review.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers, KPMG: AI semantic duplicate-request detection.

rows.act: Read submitted files to propose sample ID, entity, period, document type and source-system tags, with deterministic validation before acceptance.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers: AI extraction of evidence metadata.

rows.act: Draft a response grounded only in approved evidence and prior clarifications, leaving technical accounting conclusions and submission approval with the owner.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers: AI-drafted auditor response.

rows.act: Match each requested sample to the manifest and submitted file, exposing missing, duplicate and unmatched items before KCC submission.
rows.xc: Yes — Audit Support, process towers: Automated sample-to-evidence matching.

rows.act: Cluster adjustments and findings by process, account, entity and cause to identify recurring issues for the close-improvement backlog.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers, Accounting Policy: AI audit-adjustment root-cause clustering.

rows.act: Use ageing, clarification count and owner workload to flag requests likely to miss the audit timetable for Controller intervention.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, process towers: Predictive escalation-risk alerts.

rows.t: Automate the APAC manual journal dashboard
rows.act: Standardise the monthly BlackLine extract, Python cleansing and Power BI refresh so journal volume and root causes are available without manual file handling.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R, all posting teams: Automate the APAC manual journal dashboard.
rows.rem: Dashboard foundation exists; source import remains partly manual.

rows.t: Standardise document header text and reason codes
rows.act: Use controlled header and reason-code values so journals can be categorised consistently and analysed without manual interpretation.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R, P2P, O2C, Tax, Operations: Standardise document header text and reason codes.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Publish one governed manual journal playbook
rows.act: Define standard posting logic, templates, documentation and review requirements for major journal categories across markets.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R Global, market finance: Publish one governed manual journal playbook.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Capture root cause in BlackLine comments
rows.act: Require a structured root-cause category, requestor and approver reference for correction and reclass journals so the dashboard can show actionable causes.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, all journal preparers and approvers: Capture root cause in BlackLine comments.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Eliminate preventable journals through upstream fixes
rows.act: Assign an accountable owner and due date for late PO, mapping, master-data, policy and system causes instead of repeating the correction each close.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, P2P, R2R, O2C, master-data owners: Eliminate preventable journals through upstream fixes.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Introduce a standard journal request form
rows.act: Replace email-only intake with a controlled request form containing mandatory accounting, approval and supporting-document fields.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, market finance, Power Platform team: Introduce a standard journal request form.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.act: Validate the request before submission and prevent incomplete or non-compliant journals from entering the preparation queue.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, Global Digital: Add pre-submission journal checks.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future
rows.rem: The June target flow refers to an agentic bot with human review.

rows.t: Prioritise the highest-volume requestors and causes
rows.act: Use the dashboard to identify the markets, departments and root causes producing the largest preventable workload.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, business-unit finance: Prioritise the highest-volume requestors and causes.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Establish monthly and quarterly journal governance
rows.act: Review journal volume and remediation with CFOs monthly and AA leadership quarterly, tracking owners and repeat causes.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, CFOs, AA leadership: Establish monthly and quarterly journal governance.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Scale the dashboard across towers and regions
rows.act: Publish the same governed journal dataset for teams already posting through BlackLine so each tower can identify its own improvement opportunities.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R, C2C, P2P, Tax, Operations, regional teams: Scale the dashboard across towers and regions.
rows.st: Can be implemented in the future

rows.t: Schedule BlackLine extraction and dashboard refresh
rows.act: Use an approved API or scheduled export to remove the remaining manual BlackLine download and provide run-status evidence.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, BlackLine owner, Global Digital: Schedule BlackLine extraction and dashboard refresh.

rows.act: Check required fields, balanced debits and credits, duplicate references, valid GL and cost-centre combinations, approvals and evidence before BlackLine load.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R, master-data owners: Deterministic journal validation service.

rows.act: Suggest a root-cause category from journal text and supporting evidence, with the preparer confirming or correcting the classification.
rows.xc: No

rows.t: AI policy and playbook compliance review
rows.act: Compare each journal request with the approved playbook and surface relevant requirements or missing evidence without making the accounting decision.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, Accounting Policy: AI policy and playbook compliance review.

rows.t: AI anomaly and duplicate journal detection
rows.act: Flag unusual amounts, timing, account combinations, repeated narratives and potential duplicate postings before approval.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, R2R: AI anomaly and duplicate journal detection.

rows.act: Cluster repeat corrections by cause, requestor, market and account and propose candidate upstream fixes for owner evaluation.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, relevant process towers: AI recurring-pattern and remediation insights.

rows.act: Create a first-pass, source-cited explanation of purpose, movement and evidence for the preparer and approver to edit.
rows.xc: No

rows.act: Allow authorised users to ask which causes drive corrections or which markets repeat a journal, returning filters and source journal IDs.
rows.xc: No

rows.act: Generate a journal manifest, approval record and supporting-document index for audit samples to reduce repeated evidence assembly.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, Audit Support: Automated audit evidence package.

rows.act: Send recurring invalid mapping patterns to the relevant data steward with affected journals, impact and proposed priority.
rows.xc: Yes — Controlling, data stewards, process towers: Master-data remediation feedback loop.

rows.act: Measure hours avoided, journals eliminated and recurrence after each remediation so the 30 percent target is supported by traceable outcomes.
rows.xc: No
